page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.12xlarge is an arm64 storage-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 48 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz, with 1 thread per core and no simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources comprise 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 36 MB L3 cache. Memory provisioning sits at 384.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Storage consists of 30,000 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, while baseline network throughput is rated at 75 Gbps. This instance does not include a GPU accelerator.

Benchmark outcomes show distinct multi-threaded and memory-heavy advantages. In Geekbench testing, the instance records 23,554.0 points in multi-core metrics (top tier) and 67,152.0 points for Clang software compilation, alongside a strong stress-ng multi-core result of 81,861.57. Single-core performance falls in the average tier across stress-ng (1706.49) and Geekbench (1819.0). Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 389.45 GB/sec for large reads and 192.74 GB/sec for writes, both ranking in the top 10 percent, mirrored by a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3,251.71. Database operations score 47,318.64 on PassMark, and Redis SET throughput reaches 96.25 million operations per second, with static web serving achieving 96.06 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the dedicated physical cores and 30 TB NVMe allocation deliver high I/O and data-density per node without hyperthreading contention. However, the architecture shows lower single-threaded throughput relative to its parallel scale, and LLM text generation on smaller models is constrained by the absence of dedicated matrix or GPU acceleration. It is suited for I/O-intensive workloads including transactional databases, distributed storage arrays, search engines, real-time analytics, and large-scale parallel software build systems.
description: Amazon Web Services i8ge.12xlarge is a storage-optimized arm64 instance driven by an AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor with 48 dedicated physical cores at 2.8 GHz, 384.0 GB of memory, and 75 Gbps baseline networking. Bundled with 30,000 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and zero GPUs, the system delivers massive I/O capacity and memory throughput, clocking 389.45 GB/sec in uncached 256MB reads and 192.74 GB/sec in writes. Multi-core performance is top-tier, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 23,554.0 and 47,318.64 on PassMark database operations, while single-core performance remains average. The 8 GB RAM per core ratio and high local NVMe density provide efficient resource scaling for I/O-heavy environments. This hardware profile suits distributed NoSQL and relational databases, real-time analytics engines, data warehousing, and large parallel compilation workloads.
